sources.title: Number Portability
sources.geo: United Kingdom communications providers and customers
facts: Number portability lets customers keep a landline or mobile number when changing provider.
Ofcom links portability duties to General Conditions B3 and C7.
limits: The page states regulatory duties rather than confirming a specific port.
Portability does not prove broadband availability at an address.

sources.title: Simpler and quicker broadband switching is here
sources.geo: United Kingdom residential broadband and landline customers
facts: One Touch Switch lets customers contact only the new provider to arrange a fixed-service switch.
Providers must compensate qualifying customers if a switch delay leaves them without service for more than one working day.
limits: The process does not prove that a selected provider serves a premises.
A successful switch still depends on provider records and technical feasibility.

sources.title: Ofcom fines Virgin Media £28m for repeatedly preventing customers from cancelling contracts
facts: Ofcom imposed a £28 million penalty for serious failures in contract termination procedures.
The investigation covered likely mishandling of millions of calls between January 2022 and September 2024.
limits: The enforcement decision concerns cancellation conduct, not network coverage.
The decision does not determine every individual customer's remedy.

sources.title: What to do if your broadband or landline provider goes out of business
sources.geo: United Kingdom broadband and landline customers
facts: If another company takes over, service and contracts may transfer with limited interruption.
If no takeover occurs, customers need to arrange service with a new provider.
limits: The guidance is scenario-based and does not predict a specific provider failure.
A transferred contract does not prove address-level orderability from alternatives.

sources.title: Contracts
sources.kind: business phone and broadband contract guidance
facts: Small-business customers should receive written contract information and a contract summary before consent.
Providers must clearly disclose agreed in-contract price changes in pounds and pence.
limits: Rights depend on customer size, contract date and terms.
Contract guidance does not establish service quality or premises coverage.

sources.title: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q4 2025
sources.geo: United Kingdom major telecoms and pay-TV providers
facts: The release covers October to December 2025.
Broadband and landline complaints decreased while mobile complaints increased.
limits: Complaint volumes do not establish coverage or orderability.

sources.title: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q3 2025
sources.geo: United Kingdom major telecoms and pay-TV providers
facts: The release covers July to September 2025.
Overall complaint levels were similar to the preceding quarter.
limits: Provider complaint rates are not premises-level performance.
The figures do not resolve individual complaints.

sources.title: Enforcement programme: Industry's failure to implement One Touch Switch by deadline of 3 April 2023
facts: Ofcom closed the industry-wide programme on 11 June 2026.
The majority of customers were found to be switching successfully through One Touch Switch.
limits: Closure of the programme does not prove every provider or switch is compliant.
Switching compliance is separate from premises availability.

sources.title: 1.6 million Brits hit switch on their landline or broadband provider
facts: Ofcom reported more than 1.6 million One Touch Switch transactions in the first year.
More than 300 providers were signed up to the process.
limits: A switch count does not prove service availability for a parcel.
